paper_title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for   Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
caption: Number of questions, out of 40, where CoT generated by GPT3 using different methods has at least 1 factual error. Factual errors: < OneR < NoR.
model_annotation: This bar chart, titled "Factual Errors," displays the number of questions—out of a total of 40—for which the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generated by GPT-3 using three different methods produced at least one factual error, categorized by four datasets: HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC. The horizontal axis lists these four datasets in alphabetical order, while the vertical axis represents the count of factual errors, scaled linearly from 0 to 35 with tick marks at regular intervals of 5. Each dataset is represented by a group of three vertically stacked bars, corresponding to the three methods: NoR QA (orange with a grid pattern), OneR QA (red with a dot pattern), and IRCt QA (blue with diagonal stripes). For HotpotQA, the bars show 15 errors for NoR QA, 10 for OneR QA, and 5 for IRCt QA. For 2WikiMQA, the values are 29 for NoR QA, 23 for OneR QA, and 14 for IRCt QA. For MuSiQue, the values are 28 for NoR QA, 27 for OneR QA, and 23 for IRCt QA. For IIRC, the values are 15 for NoR QA, 14 for OneR QA, and 11 for IRCt QA. The bars are not sorted; they are presented in the order of the datasets as listed on the horizontal axis. According to the caption, factual errors are ordered such that OneR QA has fewer errors than NoR QA, and IRCt QA has fewer errors than OneR QA, which is visually consistent with the chart showing the red bars (OneR QA) consistently shorter than the orange bars (NoR QA), and the blue bars (IRCt QA) consistently shorter than the red bars across all datasets.
